facts.heading: General anxiety level
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time. This anxiety got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it got worse in September.

facts.heading: Work change in September
facts.content: Hannah's deputy head at school left. She was asked to step up in that role.
facts.evidence: It was my deputy head at my school. I've taught here for 11 years and I have loved it and then they had asked me to step up and when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of being incompetent
facts.content: Hannah keeps thinking someone will notice she has no idea what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Nighttime rehearsal behavior
facts.content: Hannah rehearses what to say and what others will think on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings, my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Fear of negative judgment
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth.

facts.heading: Fear of being replaced
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she was given the job to someone less capable.
facts.evidence: That they gave the job to a nice earful teacher who can't actually read.

facts.heading: Email rewriting behavior
facts.content: Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times last week.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of seeming stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves would think she was stupid regarding the email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Governor's treatment
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves has been kind to Hannah. He told her he was delighted in September.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind. He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling of pretense
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about her capability.
facts.evidence: I feel like I'm lying to him. About being capable, as if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Identity comparison to mother
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat. Hannah's mother was a headteacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat. My mum's, I suppose. She was a headteacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother's professional legacy
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a brilliant headteacher who was highly regarded in the village.
facts.evidence: She was brilliant. Everyone in the village still stops me to say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Mother's retirement recognition
facts.content: A library in the village is named after Hannah's mother.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago and they have named a library after her.

facts.heading: Comparing current job
facts.content: Hannah compares her current deputy role to her mother's past position.
facts.evidence: A deputy's job, but yes, I can't help comparing.

facts.heading: Mother's supportive comments
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Suppressing distress to mother
facts.content: Hannah does not tell her how bad things are because it makes her feel like she is making a fuss.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss, so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking up at 4 AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at 4 every morning going through a to-do list.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at 4 every morning. I fall asleep fine. Then I'm awake at 4 going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Drinking coffee to cope
facts.content: Hannah drinks a lot of coffee to get through the day. She knows this does not help her.
facts.evidence: I drink a lot of coffee to get through a day which I know doesn't help.

facts.heading: Drinking five or six cups
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee. This prevents her from sitting still in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: Five or six, then I can't sit still in the afternoons.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences physical symptoms in the afternoons when she is awake. Her heart goes fast and her hands shake.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms
facts.content: Hannah had to leave a meeting to splash her face with water last Thursday. She did not think anyone noticed.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday, I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water. I don't think so.

facts.heading: Feeling exhausted daily
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day. This exhaustion comes from pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day. Just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's advice
facts.content: Ben says Hannah should just enjoy things. Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when he says this.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it. Guilty and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's profession
facts.content: Ben is an engineer. He thinks if something is a problem, it can be fixed.
facts.evidence: He's an engineer. He thinks if something's a problem, you fix it.

facts.heading: Difficulty with social friends
facts.content: Hannah does not have friends at school she can talk to anymore.
facts.evidence: Not anymore, not really.

facts.heading: Lost lunch group friends
facts.content: Hannah used to eat lunch with others in the year for a quarter. She is now their line manager.
facts.evidence: I used to eat lunch in the year for a quarter with the others. Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.

facts.heading: Misses children and class
facts.content: Hannah misses the children most. She misses the daily experience of a child getting something for the first time.
facts.evidence: The children mostly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Work life is spreadsheets
facts.content: Hannah's days are spreadsheets.
facts.evidence: No, my days are spreadsheets.

facts.heading: Wanted the promotion
facts.content: Hannah thought she wanted the promotion. She said yes because she could not say no to her.
facts.evidence: I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.

facts.heading: Tears about fear
facts.content: Hannah cried after saying yes to the promotion. The tears were about fear and never getting to go back.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays. They went walking in the lakes for ten days without thinking about school.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays. We went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Wreck before term started
facts.content: The week before term started, Hannah was a wreck again. She could not eat on Sunday.
facts.evidence: The week before term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah tried writing down things that went well each evening. This practice lasted for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things, a true laughing, a good email. It held for about two weeks, and then I stopped because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Goal to do job without fraud
facts.content: Hannah wants to do her job without feeling like a fraud. This involves not rehearsing in meetings and sending only one email.
facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud. Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first. Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal for Sunday evening rest
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without stomach knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feeling after stating goals
facts.content: Hannah felt lightful and lighter, and a bit tearful after stating her goals out loud.
facts.evidence: Lightful. Lighter. A bit tearful actually.

facts.heading: First time sharing bad news
facts.content: This is the first time Hannah has told anyone how bad something is. She has not told Ben about the 4am issue.
facts.evidence: It's the first time I have told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows how about the 4am.

facts.heading: Fear of telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah feels scared about telling Ben how bad things are. She worries he would be hurt that she didn't say sooner.
facts.evidence: Scary. He would probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Strategy to share difficult news
facts.content: Hannah might try telling someone this week. She plans to choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening, perhaps Saturday morning over breakfast.
facts.evidence: If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening. then I'm too warmed up. Saturday morning, perhaps? Yeah, over breakfast.

facts.heading: Plan to try notebook again
facts.content: Hannah is considering trying the evening notebook again for a week, even just one line.
facts.evidence: Would you try the evening notebook again, just for a week? Even one line? I could.
